      23                 :             : /// For specification of the DLT protocol, please see:
      24                 :             : /// https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/user_upload/standards/foundation/1-0/AUTOSAR_PRS_DiagnosticLogAndTraceProtocol.pdf
      25                 :             : ///
      26                 :             : /// As described in chapter 5.1 the general format of an DLT message looks as follows:
      27                 :             : /// +-----------------+-----------------+---------+
      28                 :             : /// | Standard Header | Extended Header | Payload |
      29                 :             : /// +-----------------+-----------------+---------+
      30                 :             : ///
      31                 :             : /// The `Standard Header` and `Extended Header` are for now no concern in this implementation. They will be filled by
      32                 :             : /// the `DataRouter` application. For now we focus in this document on the `Payload` part.
      33                 :             : ///
      34                 :             : /// The payload section can be filled in two ways: Non-Verbose (chapter 5.1.2.1) or Verbose (5.1.2.2).
      35                 :             : /// This part of our code only implements the Verbose-Mode.
      36                 :             : ///
      37                 :             : /// The verbose mode is further split into argument sections (PRS_Dlt_00459).
      38                 :             : /// +-----------------+-----------------+-----------------------------------------------------+
      39                 :             : /// | Standard Header | Extended Header |                       Payload                       |
      40                 :             : /// |                 |                 +--------------------------+--------------------------+
      41                 :             : /// |                 |                 |        Argument 1        |        Argument 2        |
      42                 :             : /// |                 |                 +-----------+--------------+-----------+--------------+
      43                 :             : /// |                 |                 | Type Info | Data Payload | Type Info | Data Payload |
      44                 :             : /// +-----------------+-----------------+-----------+--------------+-----------+--------------+
      45                 :             : ///
      46                 :             : /// For now also this handling of argument numbers is not handled within this class. This class rather interprets each
      47                 :             : /// call to Log() as another argument that is added towards the payload. For this it takes case that the Type Info and
      48                 :             : /// Data Payload are filled correctly. Any recorder using this formatter, will for now take care of the argument
      49                 :             : /// handling.
